closing.reason: Tried to reach #1267's consequence (an operator's grants on a reshaped surface function lost by re-running install.sql) outside the diff. (1) Call sites: the five declared functions are each created exactly once in pgpm_core/install.sql (14255, 14315, 14441, 14606, 14760) and each is followed by its _surface_carry_grants call; pgpm_archive and pgpm_hypertable neither create nor reshape any of them; install.sql itself issues no grants on them; _surface_settled fails an install that leaves a kept function, so a sixth declared function without its call fails loudly. The other drop-and-recreate sites (signature-changing drops of transmute/obtain/from_hypertable etc.) change the signature, are outside the #983 surface promise the body covers, and are not this mechanism. (2) Upgrade/resume: the stopped-run path (kept exists, current function dropped only if still unreplaceable, else carried) is coherent; the only grant loss I could construct needs a downgrade to an older install.sql between a stopped run and the next, which pgpm does not document. The documented command is --single-transaction. (3) Body promises: ran on pgpm_prv-15 an older status() owned by a non-installing role with PUBLIC revoked, a grant option to v_ops and a grant v_ops made through it; after the re-run the new shape held {postgres=X/postgres, v_ops=X*/postgres, v_mon=X/v_ops} and v_ops's own REVOKE removed v_mon, so grantor and chain order are carried. The owner (and the old owner's implicit EXECUTE) is not carried, which the body's Caveats disclose. The 42501 refusal checks every grant-option grantor with the same SET/MEMBER plus USAGE rule _acl_may_grant_as uses, before anything is taken. (4) Mutations: surface_prepare_drops_granted alone restores the issue's defect (the acceptance repro fails on it); surface_carry_grants_as_owner and surface_prepare_grantor_unchecked do not, by design: they put back the grantor and the up-front refusal, sub-claims the issue repro does not exercise, and tests/336 parts A and D catch them per the PR. (5) Contract change: the only new refusal (42501) applies to grants an operator made through a grant option that the installing session cannot SET ROLE to, and the guide documents it with a remedy (run as a superuser). It is not a refusal of a documented workflow. No claim written.
